module.title: Radiographic Interpretation & AI Comparison
module.goal: Apply structured diagnostic reasoning to identify pathology, then compare, refine, and justify interpretations through AI-assisted dialogue and feedback.

objectives.text: Correctly identify common radiographic findings, including caries, bone loss, periapical lesions, and restorative defects, with ≥90% accuracy
Correctly identify the affected tooth and surface associated with a radiographic finding with ≥90% accuracy
Use radiographic evidence, including radiolucency pattern, location, border definition, and surrounding structures, to support diagnostic decisions in ≥90% of responses
Differentiate true pathology from overlapping structures, artifacts, or normal anatomy in ≥90% of cases
Compare personal diagnostic interpretations with AI-generated feedback and determine whether the AI interpretation is correct in ≥90% of cases
Appropriately accept, refine, or challenge AI-generated interpretations using radiographic evidence in ≥90% of interactions
Demonstrate improvement in diagnostic accuracy after AI dialogue or annotation review in ≥15% of applicable cases
Avoid changing a correct diagnosis to an incorrect diagnosis after AI or annotation feedback in ≥90% of applicable cases
Demonstrate improved confidence calibration by aligning confidence scores with diagnostic accuracy in ≥90% of cases

steps.prompt: Review the radiograph below. Mark the area you would like to evaluate first by placing a marker or drawing a box.
steps.expected: Area marked includes the mesial interproximal lesion on tooth #30.
steps.feedback: The selected area should include the interproximal radiolucency on the mesial surface of tooth #30.

steps.prompt: Identify the tooth associated with the selected area and select the affected surface.
steps.feedback: The selected area corresponds to tooth #30 on the mesial surface.

steps.prompt: What is the primary radiographic finding?
steps.feedback: The radiolucency on the mesial surface of tooth #30 is consistent with interproximal caries.

steps.prompt: Review the AI interpretation below. Based on your interpretation of the radiograph, how would you like to proceed?
steps.expected: Student evaluates the AI interpretation and decides whether to keep or revise the original interpretation or request AI guidance.
steps.feedback: Compare the AI interpretation with your own assessment. Use the radiographic evidence to determine whether your original interpretation should be maintained or revised.
steps.ai_interpretation: Identified Interproximal caries on the mesial surface of tooth #30.

steps.prompt: Review the annotated radiograph and faculty explanation.
steps.feedback: The annotated image demonstrates interproximal caries on the mesial surface of tooth #30. The lesion appears as a triangular radiolucency extending beyond the dentinoenamel junction. Differentiate this appearance from cervical burnout, which has diffuse borders and occurs near the cementoenamel junction.

steps.prompt: Review the radiograph below. Mark the area you would like to evaluate first by placing a marker or drawing a box.
steps.expected: Area marked includes the distal crown margin of tooth #19
steps.feedback: The selected area should include the radiolucency beneath the distal crown margin on tooth #19.

steps.prompt: Identify the tooth associated with the area you selected.
steps.feedback: The selected area corresponds to tooth #19.

steps.prompt: What is the primary radiographic finding?
steps.feedback: The radiolucency beneath the distal crown margin is consistent with recurrent caries.

steps.prompt: Review the AI interpretation below. Based on your interpretation of the radiograph, how would you like to proceed?
steps.expected: Student evaluates the AI interpretation and decides whether to keep or revise the original interpretation. If the student selects "I'm uncertain," ORBIT launches the AI Coaching workflow.
steps.feedback: Compare the AI interpretation with your own assessment. If you remain uncertain, use the AI Coaching guidance to help you arrive at your final interpretation.
steps.ai_interpretation: I identified recurrent caries beneath the distal crown margin of tooth #19.

steps.prompt: Recurrent caries on the distal surface of tooth #19 beneath the crown margin
steps.feedback: The annotated image demonstrates recurrent caries beneath the distal crown margin of tooth #19. Recurrent caries often appears as a radiolucency adjacent to an existing restoration or crown margin. Careful evaluation of restoration margins is essential to distinguish recurrent decay from restorative materials or radiographic artifacts.

expert.correct: Recurrent caries on the distal surface of tooth #19 beneath the crown margin.
expert.why: The radiolucency is located beneath the distal margin of the crown and extends into the adjacent tooth structure, a classic radiographic appearance of recurrent caries.
expert.pitfall: Students often mistake radiolucencies beneath restoration margins for restorative material, burnout, or radiographic artifact rather than recurrent caries.
expert.teaching:
Carefully evaluate all restoration and crown margins for radiolucencies.
• Compare the radiographic density beneath the restoration with the surrounding dentin.
• Correlate the radiographic appearance with the patient's caries risk and clinical findings.
expert.pearls: Always inspect restoration margins systematically—small radiolucencies beneath a crown or restoration may represent early recurrent caries before clinical symptoms develop.

cases.name: Distal Caries vs Overlap
cases.notes: Differentiate true caries from contact overlap

steps.prompt: Review the radiograph below. Mark the area you would like to evaluate first by placing a marker or drawing a box.
steps.expected: Area marked includes the distal interproximal surface of tooth #30.
steps.feedback: The selected area should include the suspicious radiolucency adjacent to the distal surface of tooth #30.

steps.prompt: Identify the tooth associated with the selected area and select the affected surface.
steps.feedback: The selected area corresponds to the distal surface of tooth #30.

steps.prompt: What is the primary radiographic finding?
steps.feedback: The radiolucency is consistent with interproximal caries rather than simple contact overlap.

steps.prompt: The AI identified contact overlap rather than caries. Based on your interpretation, would you like to accept, revise, or keep your original interpretation?
steps.expected: Student makes a clinical decision after reviewing the AI interpretation
steps.feedback: Compare the AI interpretation with the radiographic evidence before making your final decision.

steps.prompt: Review the annotated radiograph and faculty explanation.
steps.feedback: The faculty review demonstrates that the radiolucency extends beyond the normal appearance of contact overlap and is consistent with interproximal caries. Evaluate lesion shape, border definition, and extension beyond the enamel when distinguishing caries from overlap.

cases.name: Mental Foramen vs. Periapical Pathology
cases.notes: AI may incorrectly suggest periapical pathology

steps.prompt: Review the radiograph below. Mark the area you would like to evaluate first by placing a marker or drawing a box.
steps.expected: Area marked includes the radiolucency adjacent to the apex of tooth #29.
steps.feedback: The selected area should include the radiolucency in the premolar region near tooth #29.

steps.prompt: Identify the tooth associated with the selected area and select the affected surface.
steps.feedback: The selected area is associated with the apical region of tooth #29.

steps.prompt: What is the primary radiographic finding?
steps.feedback: The radiolucency is consistent with the mental foramen, a normal anatomical structure, rather than a periapical lesion.

steps.prompt: Review the AI interpretation below. Based on your interpretation of the radiograph, how would you like to proceed?
steps.expected: Student evaluates the AI interpretation and decides whether to keep or revise the original interpretation or request AI Coaching.
steps.feedback: Compare the AI interpretation with the radiographic evidence. Evaluate the position of the lamina dura, periodontal ligament space, and the location of the radiolucency before making your final decision.
steps.ai_interpretation: I identified a periapical lesion associated with tooth #29.

steps.prompt: Review the annotated radiograph and faculty explanation.
steps.feedback: The annotated image demonstrates the mental foramen, a normal anatomical landmark commonly mistaken for a periapical lesion. An intact lamina dura and normal periodontal ligament space help distinguish normal anatomy from pathology. Always correlate the radiographic appearance with the tooth's clinical status before diagnosing periapical disease.
